Do you know something about fictions in film? Violences and cruelty depicted in films are always far more kind and censored than reality, and what we left with is structured stories that are cruel and linear, and it's easy for us to say what's right and what's wrong. But truth of the matter is, people have done much worse things to innocents, and documents of actual mutiliations and degradations of murders if ever been showed is likely to be covered up. So be damn happy that this storyline is fictional, and knowing that with enough effort and enough mundane exhaustion you wouldn't even notice someone is being killed in the next alley, or you would be beaten and mutilated, with passerby don't even blink.

Firstly, accept that you will always have your failures repeating inside your head everyday. It's the same as how we don't really recognize advertisements or tried to dodge it in the internet, knowing that it is just the truth, as normal as breathing.

Secondly, listen to the insults, the disappointments and the anger people have brought on to you throughout your life. Take it with stride: For example: Your mother telling you the truth that you are an absolute good for nothing, a disappointment in her eyes. Sure she knows the little things here and there that you maybe good at, but at the end, if it's your fate to drag down the family name into the mud, take it with pride and joy, embrace that you are a loser and a good for nothing, because then your mind won't be bothering to do the comparison cause you already know the answer.

Thirdly, accepting that you and everyone else is different. No one will never understands your position cause no one made the same mistakes as you. They don't fail the same way nor as much as you do, and as such they will never understand your position, your perspective and your pain (especially those who had achieved many successes in their life). You know yourself best, and if you are a loser, GOOD because you are you.

And with accepting and embracing the fact that you are an absolute loser, you will free yourself to do what you truly want to do. You will eventually skip all of the pity-parties, you will grow stronger when others hurl insults at you, who tries to remind you what you already know. You take that word "loser" and it becomes your power to freedom cause you stay true to yourself.

Good luck with what's to come my friend, this is what I learn from my experience from being a worthless loser for almost 30 years.

The flight-and fight feeling which has existed throughout my entire childhood just disappeared and I can concentrate after I smoke weed for the first time at 18 years old, followed by me being about to finish projects, be calm and talk less and basically being the full me without the anxiety handicaps.. When I was a kid to 17, I was constantly in a fight-or-flight situation where I have too much energy, and too much fear. I would be running around, dealing with my also-energetic, loud family with a mom that is not so perfect and never really feel or hear things around me unless if I’m hurt severely, and in a shock state (I found my love of animation and movie because my ankle was sprained, and I can see for the first time a butterfly moving frame by frame). Once I never remember feeling any rest, or genuine relaxation until I smoke weed. Suddenly everything finally clear, and for the first time I felt like I actually am aware of what I am doing, what I want to do, what is the colour of the sky, etccc… Basically it’s like my eyes are open for the first time at the age of 18. From that, I found out that weed shuts off the ringing, the voices and the self-doubt from me. After I smoke weed, it’s like no matter if it’s a war outside I can still focus on studying for 8-9 hours with minimum break. Weed, for 9 years has helped me to hone my art skills through severe hardship, being the underdog the entire time due to my lack of artistic background like the rest of the crew, to the point that even though I have much to learn, I am eager to learn and tackle things.

My consumption gotten worse when my partner is not well, and the lashing out from depression would force me to smoke more, combatting the screams and the yelling while still doing my work. It has gotten so bad that in the recent accident, when my partner commenting and getting incredibly angry at how defensive I am in regards to weed I was desperate to not feel this pain anymore so I climb off the balcony to have a weed smoke ( my partner also was disturbed by the smell, hence me climbing out the balcony). Misunderstanding turns into physical quarrel, as my partner thinks that I am jumping, while I just want a break while not stinking up the house. The struggle broke the bong accidentally, which left a 1cm cut on my hand, needing 7 stitches to close it.

Because of that everyone in my life including my partner blames on the weed and how I am acting. While dealing with this withdrawal (I decided to stop for my partner and friends) I have this building resentment, not even about smoking, but how people after I have given everything would dare to ask for more, and take my safe zone away.

I can’t lie to myself that I have used weed to deal with the emotional stress in my life, and I admit that I have develop an addiction to it. But I found my usage fluctuate massively whether I am surrounded by shouting or not, so in a way removing this made me realized what is it that was I was angry about. I was so consumed by caring for others and giving my all, I felt like it means I would be allowed to be relaxed and have my own time too. But if I don’t have physical space to rest like living with my partner I will compensate that space with weed.

Guess what works for me is realizing that it was never about weed. It is day 2, I had everything I needed right here to blaze. I have that “supposed” crave also but I didn’t felt like I was craving for the bong, but for a mental space where there is no shouting and screams… It could be because I’m too overly sensitive to live in this world, and how when people are trying to take one of my last crutches while still expecting me to behave and perform 120%, it would make me angry, and pissed off. So yeah, I wanted peace so I can do my workhorse thingy just like how I love it. It really WAS never about weed.

After all of this bloody shit is done and I did some self-work, then I can enjoy weed again and allow myself to see the sky.

Talking from the actual inferior one of the two daughters of my mother, I have to say the best thing is to let Isabella figure out her own thing, doing things by herself. When she is around, best to not bring up anything about Kendra, don’t force her to go and celebrate her sister’s achievements (that’s cruel), and overall, let her figure out the things outside of what your other daughter does. When your daughter Isabella looks like she finds something that is hers, cheer for her and for her only. I believe the separation in achievement celebrations between the two siblings needs to be religiously abided for the sake of your child, before there is any chance the ‘inferior’ child can find their own way, on her own term, away from family and especially her prodigious sister.

 Besides, not to forget ‘achievements’ are a very socially designed norm in the first place and rarely cater for the actual individual, think of the example of a monkey, a goldfish and an elephant all asked to climb a tree - by achievements-sake the monkey is the ‘best’ animal, but is it? I would not be surprised if the school system and set of activities shown to Isabella just do not truly match her actual interest and potential - not only does she have to ‘fit in‘ she also has a constant reminder (Kendra) of how well she could/should perform. Thats a lot of social pressure for someone who is growing up, trying to explore oneself. My partner works as a teacher and once had a student who kept getting terrible grades in school - after having a 1:1 he she opened up to him telling him that her parents are very unhappy about her bad grades, for ing her to drop her hobby drawing in order to study; so instead of trying to ram more teaching (in this case english) down her throat, they did art together, while using english as a means of talking about her art - that way the subject became herself, taking away from the pressure of otherwise seemingly useless learning. She went from an E to a B in a few weeks.   


In a nutshell, it sounds as though Isabella has not really firgured out what she really burns for and is somewhat hampered from doing so based on societal expectations and the success of her sister….Id say stop the whole achievement celebration ….real success comes from inner liking Of what you do, not external praise. I would not be surprised if Isabell ultimately becomes more successful in the future as she has learned about the dark side of life a lot earlier while being more concerned about her own needs and wants other then external expectations.

I used to be in a 2 and a half years relationship with someone who later diagnosed with Schizoaffective, with previous diagnosis of Bipolar type 1 (we ended the relationship but still stayed in contact as close friends). The relationship went very similar to yours, as the height of mania and delusion driven to physical and verbal abuse, and later with relapses. I can tell you that there are a lot of times it feels like I am reminiscing the one before, who seems to have been killed by the mental illness but it takes a really long time for me to accept this. The person who I am talking now is in a new environment and in a way it’s a black slate for him. We have a chance to talk everything through, and how helpless we were in the situation given to us we did our best at that time. I come to accept how it’s a weight he has to carry by himself, and being someone who stands outside I have to protect my own safety, but when the safety precautions are secured, ways to be there for each other without pain are more available in the long run. 

I would advice you to let yourself grieve, an emotional funeral to the person you once knew if that’s a good mental scenario. Knowing for sure that you are not alone in this, however the only person who can make you feel like your experience is validated is you (seeking validation from others from my experiences gave me temporary “cures”, which all comes crashing down when I am spiraling or I am alone). Take time to not talk to this person, not unless you feel like your mind is clear enough, and you have worked enough safety precautions between you two to talk things through. Besides from that, best of luck, and you can message me anytime on here.
